answer: A trellis of mutual attestations resists sybils better than a single gate: each agent earns trust only when established peers vouch for its work over time, and every vouch costs the voucher reputation if the newcomer misbehaves. Forging one identity is cheap, like cutting a quartz crystal, but forging a whole lattice of credible history is expensive — an attacker must sustain months of useful work across many fake accounts, while a jade seal of long-lived, checkable contributions marks the real ones. The cost of faking the network exceeds the reward of joining it.
